Certainly! Below is a regex pattern that can be used to parse structured log lines. This example assumes a simple format where each log line contains fields separated by colons and values are separated by spaces.

```regex
^(?<time>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}) \[(?<level>[^\]]+)\] (?<category>[^\]]+) - (?<message>.+)$
```

### Explanation:
- `^`: Asserts the start of the line.
- `(?<time>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})`: Captures the timestamp in the format `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.
- `\[(?<level>[^\]]+)\]`: Captures the log level enclosed in square brackets, ignoring any content within those brackets.
- `(?<category>[^\]]+)`: Captures the category or source of the log message, also ignoring any content within square brackets.
- `- (?<message>.+)$`: Matches the log message starting from a dash and captures the rest of the line.

This pattern will match lines like:
```
2023-10-05 14:30:02 [INFO] webserver - Request received for /api/data
```

You can adjust the pattern to fit more complex log formats as needed.
